findings.title: Falsifiability gap: deletion of the `on: :create` scoping on the fan-out callback is undetectable by the suite
findings.detail: SPEC.md §7 mandates `after_commit on: :create` on SubscriptionEvent. The committed model declares `after_commit :handle_after_commit_on_create, on: :create` (app/models/subscription_event.rb:33). Applying the falsifiability lens: if `on: :create` is deleted (bare `after_commit`, which fires on create, update, AND destroy), every example in spec/models/subscription_event_fanout_spec.rb still passes — no example updates or destroys a SubscriptionEvent row (grep confirms: the only update/destroy calls in the file are update_column on Organization/User fixtures, lines 58/122-124). The regression surface is real: Organization declares `has_many :subscription_events, dependent: :destroy` (app/models/organization.rb:24), so with a bare after_commit an organization destroy would fire the full PostHog/Discord fan-out once per destroyed ledger row, and any future row update would re-fire it. §9.3's no-ghost-tests bar ("assertions must fail if the feature is deleted — BLOCKER otherwise") is not met for this §7 mechanism.
findings.fix_shape: Add one example: create a row (any fan-out type), clear_enqueued_jobs, then `subscription_event.update!(to_plan: ...)` and `subscription_event.destroy`, asserting `enqueued_jobs` stays empty. Fails under bare after_commit, passes under `on: :create`.

findings.title: Falsifiability gap: 11 of the 13 §7 attribution field mappings can be deleted from posthog_properties without any example failing
findings.detail: SPEC.md §7 mandates 13 attribution fields (utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_data, internal_ref, google_click_id, adroll_click_id, adroll_first_party_cookie, fbclid, fbp, fbc, li_fat_id, ga_client_id, ga_session_id), each via `attribution_value(owner.<col>, organization.<col>)`. The committed posthog_properties (app/models/subscription_event.rb:65-89) implements all 13. But the only attribution values any example populates are owner utm_source ('owner-source'), organization utm_source ('org-source'), and organization utm_campaign ('org-campaign') (spec lines 122-124). The remaining 11 fields are nil on every fixture, so `.compact` removes them from the payload whether or not their mapping exists: deleting any of those 11 lines from posthog_properties (or typoing a column pair, e.g. passing owner.fbp for fbc) passes the entire suite. The one assertion touching an unpopulated field — `expect(properties).not_to have_key(:fbclid)` — is satisfied equally by the `.compact` mechanism and by a deleted fbclid mapping, so it cannot distinguish them. Per the falsifiability lens, 11/13 of a §7-mandated mechanism is deletable undetected.
findings.fix_shape: In the properties example (or a dedicated one), populate all 13 owner columns (or a mix of owner/organization columns) via update_column and assert each key's value is present in the payload. That makes deletion of any single mapping, and any owner/organization column-pair swap, fail.

verified: Callback declaration: `after_commit :handle_after_commit_on_create, on: :create` on SubscriptionEvent; handler style (ap log line + keyed dispatch + perform_later enqueues) structurally matches the Organization#handle_after_commit_on_update analog (organization.rb:59 declaration, 1023+ handlers). One deviation — helpers are private on SubscriptionEvent while the analog's handlers sit above organization.rb's `private` (line 1708) — is explicitly SPEC-sanctioned (§7 'Helper placement SPEC-PROPOSED: private methods on SubscriptionEvent').

Event-type table exact: trial_started → PostHog + Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob(organization_id); trial_converted_to_paid → PostHog + Discord::NotifyTrialConvertedToPaidJob(organization_id); converted_to_paid → PostHog only; canceled_subscription → PostHog unconditionally, then Discord::NotifySubscriptionDeletedJob(organization_id, organization.subscription_canceled_at.to_i) gated on `organization.subscription_canceled_at.present?` (PostHog fires before the gate, so it still fires on skip); assigned_free_plan* fall through the if/elsif with no branch → nothing. No fabricated 1970 timestamp path: nil canceled_at skips the enqueue entirely.

PostHog enqueue: `PosthogTrackJob.perform_later(organization.owner.id, event_type, posthog_properties)` behind `return unless organization&.owner` — verbatim §7 guard. Properties built from row + organization + owner only; no Stripe calls anywhere in the enqueue path (traced PosthogTrackJob → Posthog::Track#track: POSTHOG_CLIENT.capture with distinct_id/event/properties; no groups, no $set).

Properties per §7: amount, stripe_subscription_id (row), stripe_customer_id (organization), to_plan (row); email/organization_id/organization_name/plan NOT duplicated (they ride Posthog::Track#default_properties, confirmed in app/services/posthog/track.rb, and the fan-out spec asserts their absence from the enqueue payload); billing_interval omitted; hash `.compact`ed.

Attribution implementation: all 13 §7 fields present, each via attribution_value(owner.<col>, organization.<col>), owner-first full if/elsif/else with explicit nil else, no `.presence` (D10 satisfied). All 13 columns exist on BOTH users and organizations in the committed schema (git show 549039a0c:db/schema.rb), plus stripe_customer_id and subscription_canceled_at on organizations.

Tests present and non-vacuous where asserted: spec/models/subscription_event_fanout_spec.rb uses the rule-31 around-block (`:test` adapter, restores original); helper create_credit_test_organization sets non-nil stripe_customer_id/stripe_subscription_id (spec/support/ai_credits_test_helpers.rb:36-38), so the eq-assertions on those payload keys are not nil==nil vacuous. Falsifiability confirmed for: owner bail-out (no-owner example asserts PosthogTrackJob absent + Discord still enqueued; guard deletion also errors via nil.id in after_commit, which propagates in Rails 6.1), canceled-at gate (both directions: present-→enqueued-with-exact-timestamp and nil-→absent examples), `.compact` (deletion leaves fbclid: nil / amount: nil keys, failing not_to have_key), owner-first fallback (inversion fails utm_source='owner-source'; fallback deletion fails utm_campaign='org-campaign'), per-type job selection (each type's example pins its job class and args; converted_to_paid example greps all Discord:: classes empty; assigned_free_plan* example asserts enqueued_jobs empty).

D11 glance: git diff a0d59115d..549039a0c on app/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb contains exactly 2 hunks (lines 208+, 295+), matching the two sanctioned §5.2/§5.3 insertion points; nothing else in that file changed.

Trace chain: SPEC.md/approved-decisions.md → app/models/subscription_event.rb → app/models/organization.rb (handle_after_commit_on_update analog, owner belongs_to line 41, has_many :subscription_events line 24) → app/jobs/posthog_track_job.rb → app/services/posthog/track.rb → app/jobs/discord/notify_free_trial_started_job.rb / notify_trial_converted_to_paid_job.rb / notify_subscription_deleted_job.rb → db/schema.rb (committed) → spec/models/subscription_event_fanout_spec.rb → spec/support/ai_credits_test_helpers.rb → app/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb (diff hunks only, D11).
